home.houseHeading: Twelve rooms. Four hundred acres. No agenda.
home.houseIntro: Craigmore House sits where the glen narrows and the road gives up — a Victorian shooting lodge rebuilt around the things that matter: open fires, deep baths, a kitchen that answers to the estate rather than to fashion, and silence of a quality you will want to take home.
home.exteriorAlt: The house from the south lawn
home.diningQuote: The larder is the glen itself — the river, the hill, and a walled garden that has fed this house since 1847.
home.locationHeading: Ninety minutes from Edinburgh. A world from anywhere.
home.locationIntro: Off the A9 at Pitlochry, four miles up a single-track road that ends at our gates. Direct trains from London, Edinburgh and Inverness; we collect from the platform. The last half mile is gravel, hills, and the growing suspicion that you have made an excellent decision.
home.finalHeadingLine1: The glen will still be here.

about.title: A house with opinions
about.subtitle: Built 1847. Rebuilt around comfort, cooking and quiet ever since.
about.historyP1: Craigmore was built as a shooting lodge by a Dundee jute baron with more money than restraint, which explains the turret. For a century it hosted shooting parties, jealous cousins and at least one scandal the village still references.
about.historyP2: The present custodians bought the house in 2019 and spent three years doing the unglamorous things first — roof, pipes, kitchen — before opening twelve rooms in 2022. The brief, pinned to the office wall, has not changed: a house that feels inherited rather than designed, food that needs no adjectives, and staff who remember your name before you have repeated it.
about.historyP3: The turret, for the record, is now the smallest reading room in Scotland. The scandal remains unconfirmed.
about.ethosQuote: Luxury is not gold taps. Luxury is silence, a fire someone else lit, and dinner that knows where it came from.
about.ethosAttribution: The brief, 2019 — still on the office wall
about.sustainabilityP1: We heat the house with a biomass boiler fed by our own woodland, draw water from our own spring, and grow a meaningful share of the kitchen’s vegetables inside the 1847 wall. What we cannot grow, we buy within forty miles where the quality allows — and it usually does.
about.sustainabilityP2: No single-use plastics in the rooms, two EV chargers in the courtyard, and a rewilding plan for the upper glen that the grouse have opinions about. We publish the numbers annually rather than the slogans.

contact.title: Talk to the house
contact.subtitle: A person answers. Usually Isla. Always within one working day.

dining.title: Cooking that answers to the glen
dining.subtitle: One dining room, thirty covers, a kitchen fed by the river, the hill and a walled garden planted in 1847.
dining.philosophyHeading: Nothing arrives by motorway if it can walk from the garden.
dining.philosophyBody: The menu is written daily, in pencil, after the kitchen has spoken to the gardener, the ghillie and the weather. Venison from the hill, salmon when the river allows, vegetables that were soil-side at dawn. The wine cellar leans old-world; the whisky shelf leans local; the portions lean generous.
dining.tastingDishAlt: A dish from the tasting menu
dining.menusIntro: Sample menus — the kitchen rewrites them daily, and the glen has final approval.
dining.libraryTableBody: Twelve seats, one long oak table, and the library fire at your back. The room takes birthdays, board awaydays and proposals with equal discretion — the kitchen will build a menu around the occasion, and the sommelier will overdeliver. Bookable for lunch or dinner, residents and non-residents alike.
dining.chefBioSuffix: His tasting menu — six courses, whole table, no theatrics — has become the quiet reason a number of guests time their stays around dinner.
dining.chefQuote: I don’t have a style. I have a postcode.

experiencesPage.title: Days, properly spent
experiencesPage.subtitle: Everything below starts at the front door and is arranged by the house. Bring boots; we have the rest.
experiencesPage.intro: Four hundred acres earn their keep. The river holds salmon, the hill holds deer, the cellar holds the estate blend, and the team holds firm opinions on the correct order in which to enjoy them. Book ahead or decide at breakfast — both work.

experienceDetail.askAtDesk: Staying with us? Ask at the desk — same-day is often possible.

giftVouchers.title: Give someone the glen
giftVouchers.subtitle: Posted in proper envelopes with wax we take slightly too seriously, or emailed within the hour.
giftVouchers.intro: All vouchers are valid for eighteen months, exchangeable against anything the house does, and transferable — generosity should not come with small print. Order by phone, email or the enquiry form, and we will arrange payment and delivery the same day.
giftVouchers.phonePrefix: Prefer to order by phone? Call
giftVouchers.phoneSuffix: — vouchers ordered before 2pm catch the day’s post.

journalPage.title: Notes from the glen
journalPage.subtitle: The garden, the kitchen, the hill and the house — written by the people who keep them.

location.postcodeSuffix: — then follow the stone herons, not the satnav’s despair.

offersPage.title: Reasons, if you need one
offersPage.subtitle: Every offer below is exclusive to direct bookings — the agencies get our rack rates and our regards.

roomsPage.title: Rooms & suites
roomsPage.subtitle: Twelve rooms, no two alike, every one facing something worth waking up to.
roomsPage.intro: Every room comes with breakfast, the run of four hundred acres, and housekeeping that believes in hospital corners. Suites add space and sitting rooms; Classics add the particular smugness of having chosen well for less.

weddings.title: One wedding. The whole house.
weddings.subtitle: We host a handful of weddings a year, never more than one at a time, and never two the same.
weddings.exclusiveUseP1: When you marry at Craigmore, the house is yours: all twelve rooms, the lawns, the library, the dining room, the staff. Your guests wake up where the party ended. Our events team — which is to say, Eleanor and whoever she deems worthy — handles everything from celebrant to ceilidh band, with one planning visit each season and an opinion available whenever asked.
weddings.exclusiveUseP2: Exclusive-use weekends from £18,000 including all accommodation. Licensed for ceremonies indoors and out.
weddings.weddingTableAlt: A wedding table dressed in the dining room
weddings.southLawnDetail: Ceremonies under open sky with the glen as witness. A marquee takes the weather question off the table; the view refuses to be upstaged either way.
weddings.diningRoomDetail: Candlelit dinners at long tables, the fire lit, the kitchen cooking the best wedding food either of your families will admit to having eaten.
weddings.libraryDetail: For the small and serious: an intimate ceremony by the fire, a dram for the witnesses, and dinner to follow. Elopements handled with enthusiasm.
weddings.beginBody: Wedding viewings run most weekdays and include lunch — we believe in showing you the kitchen’s work early. Dates for the coming two years are released each January.
